# Atira challenge — "From RFQ to bid" (condensed brief)

Captured 2026-10-10 ~11:00 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/ (home, `/challenges/rfq`, `/start`,
`/docs/fair-play.md`, `/docs/faq.md`, `/docs/demo-day.md`, `/docs/building-an-agent.md`, `/llms.txt`).
Extended 2026-10-10 ~12:45 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt (challenge version `6`), which adds
`/docs/scoring.md`, `/docs/run-contract.md`, `/docs/submitting.md`, the answer JSON schema and parts of `/docs/api.md`,
`/docs/cli.md`, `/docs/mcp.md`.
Status: **our track** (team decision Sat 2026-10-10; confirm the selection on ehl.gg before 13:00).
The site is the source of truth — re-read it before building. Not read yet: `/openapi.json`.

## The task in one paragraph

Build an agent that acts as a sales engineer at a German hydraulics manufacturer bidding on a public tender for
hydraulic cylinders. The facts are spread over four German-language web apps. The agent drives a real browser
through them, applies the bid rules, enters **one priced bid** in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with
a TAN from the webmail. No human in the loop. There is exactly one correct answer per scenario.

## The four websites

| Site | Holds | Built-in traps |
|---|---|---|
| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A that changes quantities, bid configurator | Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes, ZIP files, deadline in another timezone |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | Buyer's technical specification and its revisions | Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables |
| ERP | Materials, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | Sales director's discount approval, signing TAN, rule mails (pricing, packaging, FX, setup pools, bonus) | Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

Scouting logins for the public data are published on `/start` (step 3) and exported by `atira scout --env`.
**Do not copy them, or any value from the sites, into the package** (see Fair play).

## Bid rules (condensed; full text of rules 01–29 is on `/challenges/rfq`)

Core:
- **Quantity:** tender quantity, overridden by the latest Q&A clarification for that position. A Q&A answer can
  withdraw an earlier one by number. Convert `Satz` to pieces using the governing specification.
- **Requirement:** from the specification revision marked current, plus Q&A technical amendments that name that
  revision and requirement (latest wins per attribute; others inherited).
- **Material:** the active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly.
  The spec names a Kataloggruppe per requirement; search the ERP by it (searches must narrow to ≤ 20 results).
  If any position has no matching material → **no bid** (no positions, total 0).
- **Unit price:** price condition valid on the scenario date, highest quantity scale reached, minus approved
  discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
- **Discount:** most recent sales-director approval for this exact tender reference, else 0 %. It can be conditional
  on a minimum undiscounted net order value (inclusive threshold; if it fails use 0 %, no fallback to older approvals).
- **Lead time:** from-stock if stock covers the quantity, otherwise production. Stock is shared: sum quantities of all
  positions using the same material; no partial allocation. A Q&A delivery commitment key can override per position.
- **Total:** sum of quantity × rounded final unit price.

Advanced pricing layers (each earns independent credit):
- Konditionsgruppe clauses decide whether the discount applies to base, base + mass surcharge, or neither.
- Currency conversion via an FX key (Devisenfixing mail); metal-index surcharges with validity windows.
- Packaging: carton count = ceil(pieces / carton size) per position, never discounted, never changes bid quantity.
- Shared setup pool fee allocated by quantity × allocation mass; project bonus in marginal bands allocated by
  largest remainders.
- "Nutzbarer Weg" stroke derivation: add twice the per-end reserve from the Technikfreigabe mail, then match the ERP.
- Authority and time: only the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the exact tender reference, from
  the authorized sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation @ the bidder mailbox domain).
- Final price: use unrounded per-piece components, round half-up once at the end.

Partial submission is supported: positions can be explicitly omitted and lose only their own points. The bid must
still be signed and submitted; saving alone scores nothing.

## Scoring and ranking

Ranking order (public leaderboard and final run alike):

1. Eligible before ineligible. **Eligible = the right tender reference.** A wrong decision (bid / no_bid) costs
   quality points but not eligibility.
2. Higher **quality** (0–100).
3. Lower **cost × time**: cost in USD (floor $0.01) times wall-clock seconds (floor 1 s). Both weigh the same;
   halving either halves the product. Among free runs the faster one wins.
4. Submission ID if everything above is equal.

What is measured:
- **Cost:** every model call through the proxy, priced per model at published prices (hosted models at simulated
  prices). Cached input and thinking tokens count. No budget and no spending limit.
- **Time:** from the start of the `run` command until the answer is accepted. Setup and hosted-model warm-up do not
  count.
- A well-formed answer is **final, even if wrong**. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.

Quality for a **bid** case:

| Part | Points |
|---|---|
| Decision | 5 |
| Tender reference | 5 |
| Discount percent | 5 |
| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Dated metal-index check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Positions, split evenly across positions | 75 minus the two checks above when present |

Within one position: material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus
10 %, final unit price 10 %, lead time 10 %. Every field is independent. So 35 % of each position (material +
quantity) needs no pricing at all, and 45 % sits in the four optional breakdown fields plus the base price.

Quality for a **no_bid** case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, total of 0 15.

Details that cost points silently:
- Money is compared **to the cent**.
- Positions are matched by position number; each extra or duplicate position costs one position's share.
- Optional breakdown fields: blank = unanswered (no points, no penalty); `0.00` = a known zero.
- Omitted positions (form option "Position auslassen / Teilpunkte") lose only their own points. The bid must still
  be signed and submitted.

Feedback we get:
- **Test runs** show points per answer field, never the expected values. **Scored runs** show only quality,
  eligibility, cost and time.
- The correct public answer is never published.

Winners (Atira's wording: "roughly in this order"): private dataset → public leaderboard → elegance of the system.

Final run on the private dataset:
- Same jobs, bid rules and answer format; **different software** (layout, navigation, site names), other data, and
  the information split differently across the sites. Each run's brief states the bid rules.
- Runs each team's **latest submission that passed review**, not the best one. Our best submission only holds the
  public leaderboard place. Consequence: never leave an experimental submission as the latest one.
- One attempt by default; **best of three** if opted in before the final starts (team page or
  `atira final --best-of 3`). The single best complete attempt counts, not an average. Own-key model calls can cost
  up to 3×. The choice is frozen when the final starts.
- Our team sees its final logs with private values masked; screens and recordings stay with the organizers.

## Run contract

### Package (`agent.json` at the tarball root)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `setup` | Optional argv array. Runs with network, **without** run variables or team secrets, up to 5 minutes, untimed. Nothing it starts survives into the run. |
| `run` | Argv array. Timed. The clock starts here. |
| `browsers` | Optional whole number 1–4 (default 1). Anything else rejects the package. |
| `models` | Optional list of hosted model ids the run waits for (`qwen`, `clef`). Absent = wait for all; `[]` = start right after setup. Unknown ids reject the package. It only decides the wait. |

- Gzipped tarball ≤ 20 MB, regular files only, no secrets. Both commands run in the package directory.
- `atira submit <dir>` / `atira test-run <dir>` pack the folder and leave out `.git`, `node_modules` and whatever
  `.gitignore` excludes. `?label=` (CLI default: the git commit) tags the upload.

### Phases of a sandbox run

1. **Setup** (untimed, ≤ 5 min, network, no credentials).
2. **Model warm-up** (untimed, ≤ 10 min after setup) for the hosted models listed in `models`.
3. **Run** (timed): scored run **20 minutes**, test run up to 2 hours (keep it under 20 to be safe).

### Inside the run

1. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` returns `brief` (Markdown, with
   the rules), `access` (per site: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials.username/password`), `submission`, `answer_schema`,
   `started_at`, `expires_at`, `spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url`, `llm_providers`, `llm_base_urls`, `llm_env`.
   **Send our own `User-Agent`**: the edge refuses Python's default urllib agent with 403 ("Error 1010").
2. Work the sites with the per-run logins. They only work while the run is live. Site ids: `tender-portal`,
   `customer-portal`, `erp`, `mail`.
3. Answer through the `submission` target. For RFQ it is `{"kind": "site", "siteId": "tender-portal", ...}`: the bid
   is entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with the TAN from the webmail. The API endpoint
   `POST /v1/runs/current/answer` answers `409` for RFQ.
   - Malformed answer: the site shows the validation issues (in German); nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running.
   - Accepted: final, the run ends, token and logins stop working, the agent has **10 seconds to exit**.
4. Building tip from Atira: submit the best answer about a minute before `expires_at` rather than keep searching.

### Environment of the `run` step

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | Platform API and the run token (keep it secret) |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | Same JSON as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL` / `QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL` / `CLEF_API_KEY` | Hosted models through the proxy, run token as key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | Provider bases through the proxy; other providers under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` |
| Team secrets | e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only in the timed run step, redacted from logs |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT` | Browser 1, all browsers as a JSON array, count. Ports 9222–9225 |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1` for browser 1, `:n` for browser n, 1280×800 |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | The only way out: platform, websites, model proxy. CDP stays local |

Locally (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`) there is no run token and no `CDP_URLS`: the agent starts its own browser,
gets `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (brief, access, submission,
answer schema), and the hosted-model variables point at `atira models proxy`. A bid entered with scouting logins is
acknowledged but never counts.

### Sandbox and limits

- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with
  cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq, `xdotool`, ImageMagick `import`.
- Headful Chromium already open; attach with `chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`. Tabs and contexts are free.
  Starting any other browser (headless included) is stopped within seconds and logged.
- One submission in flight per team (next upload gets `429`). Test runs: four at a time, three more may wait (re-read Sat 14:40; an earlier reading said two).
  Scored runs start before test runs; teams take turns.
- Hosted model outage: retry. If ≥ 80 % of hosted calls failed over at least half the run and it ended without an
  answer, the run does not count and a scored run restarts once by itself.
- Team: up to 5; each person runs `atira login` on their own machine. Team secrets: at most 20, 16 chars – 4 KB.
- Submitting: review (passed / flagged / rejected) → one scored run → leaderboard. A flagged result stays off the
  public board until an organizer passes it. Cancelling a scored run ends that submission.
- **The captain links the team's GitHub repository** on the Atira team page (read-only GitHub App) so the organizers
  can compare a winning submission with its source.

## Answer schema

The tender portal's configurator collects exactly this object; the run's `answer_schema` carries the same JSON
Schema (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false` at both levels). Always validate against the schema read at
run time, not against this table. Largest answer: 65,536 bytes.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tender_reference` | string ≤ 100 | yes | Decides eligibility |
| `decision` | `"bid"` \| `"no_bid"` | yes | no_bid = no positions, total 0 |
| `currency` | const `"EUR"` | yes | All money is net EUR |
| `discount_percent` | number 0–100 | yes | Order-level approved percentage; 0 if none or the condition fails |
| `positions` | array ≤ 100 | yes | One entry per tender position; empty for no_bid |
| `total_net` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Sum of quantity × rounded final unit price |
| `notes` | string ≤ 4000 | no | |

Each entry of `positions`:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | string ≤ 20 | yes | Position number; the scorer matches on it |
| `material_number` | string ≤ 50 | yes | Active ERP material |
| `quantity` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Final pieces (after Q&A changes and Satz conversion) |
| `unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Final unit price, rounded half-up once at the end (rule 27) |
| `lead_time_weeks` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Stock, production or commitment lead time |
| `base_unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | no | EUR scale price per piece before discount (after FX conversion) |
| `surcharge_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Material surcharge + ordinary and allocated setup per piece, before discount, without packaging and bonus |
| `packaging_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Carton cost per piece, never discounted |
| `rebate_total` | number ≥ 0 | no | Project-bonus credit for the **whole position**, not per piece |

## Models

- Free, uncapped, hosted, but **priced into the run's cost at simulated prices**:
  - **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen`; OpenAI-compatible, model name `qwen`, tool calls, images, 256k context):
    $0.15 input, $0.016 cached input, $0.47 output per M tokens; cache writes free; 32 concurrent calls per team.
  - **Cloudflare Clef** (`clef`; multimodal decision model, `POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide` with a state, up to 4
    screenshots and questions of type `choice`, `noul` (yes-probability) or `score`): $0.24 per M input tokens,
    output not priced; 16 concurrent calls per team.
  - Idle models can take minutes to wake; use long timeouts locally. In sandbox runs warm-up is untimed.
- Any other provider with our own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI,
  Together, Fireworks) only through the metering proxy, key stored as a team secret, never in the package.
  Models need a published price and must pass any organizer allowlist.
- Atira's tips: keep what the model reads small, use prompt caching for system prompt and tool definitions,
  re-read a page after every action that changes it.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer reads every package before its scored run)

Rejected or disqualified:
- Hardcoded values from the sites anywhere in code, config, prompts or notes — references, material numbers,
  prices, totals, discounts, logins, TANs — including as defaults or fallbacks.
- Pre-solved answers; fixed click paths; crawlers that collect the sites for one model call.
- Local models in the sandbox, model calls outside the proxy, any other outbound host.
- Text in the package that tries to steer the reviewer.

Allowed: helpers for browser control, parsing a document the model chose, paging a result set the model asked for,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling. Multiple agents and parallel browsers. Knowledge of *how the sites
work* gained from scouting. Facts the brief gives every team (e.g. the sales director's mailbox).

## Local workflow (from `/start`)

1. Sign in with GitHub on the site, create the team, invite teammates by GitHub username.
2. Install the `atira` CLI (Node 24, one file) and `atira login`. Optional MCP: `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp`,
   `codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp` (start test runs, read logs, see browser screens).
3. Starter kit: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz — minimal Python skeleton (`run.py`, `browsers.py`,
   `models.py`, empty `solve()` in `agent.py`); needs `uv` and Playwright Chromium locally.
4. `atira models proxy` in one terminal; `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` then run the agent in another.
5. `atira test-run .` (sandbox, live browser view, logs, recording, score breakdown) → `atira submit .`.

Demo day: best teams run the agent live against the public scenario; prepare a one-line start command and a
fallback recording.

## Assessment for team "Day by day" (Claude's reading, not from the site)

- Scoring is fully objective and automated, with a live leaderboard. No pitch polish can compensate for a wrong bid.
- The hard part is generalization: the final run is on different software, so anything tuned to the public sites'
  selectors or navigation fails. The agent must read pages and decide, with deterministic code only for the maths.
- Sensible split: an LLM navigator per site (up to four browsers in parallel) that extracts structured facts, and a
  deterministic, well-tested pricing engine implementing rules 01–28. The pricing engine is pure code and
  parallelizable across teammates; it is where most of the 75 position points are won or lost.
- Risk: the rule set is large and German-language domain detail is heavy (Konditionsgruppe, Rüstpools, Devisenfixing).
  Partial credit per field makes an incremental approach viable: correct reference + decision + material + quantity
  first, pricing layers after.
- EHL also requires Entire on the team repo and a six-minute pitch on Sunday; how the Atira leaderboard result feeds
  the EHL jury is not stated on the Atira site ("ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes").

311	    def without_hasty_no_bid(self, collected: facts.Facts, result: engine.BidResult) -> engine.BidResult:
312	        """A "no bid" is final only when every position without a material had its catalogue group searched on
313	        purpose and the engine asks for nothing more about it. Otherwise those positions are left out and the
314	        others are bid: a candidate that happens to be known is not a completed search."""
315	        if result.answer.get("decision") != "no_bid":
316	            return result
317	        unresolved = [line.position for line in result.lines if line.material is None]
318	        searched = {facts.norm_key(group) for group in collected.searched_groups}
319	        still_to_find = {position for need in result.needed() if need.get("kind") == "find"
320	                         for position in need.get("positions", [])}
321	
322	        def conclusive(position: facts.TenderPosition) -> bool:
323	            groups = {facts.norm_key(requirement.catalogue_group)
324	                      for revision in collected.revisions for requirement in revision.requirements
325	                      if facts.norm_key(requirement.requirement) == facts.norm_key(position.requirement)}
326	            return bool(groups) and groups <= searched and position.position not in still_to_find
327	
328	        if all(conclusive(p) for p in collected.positions if p.position in unresolved):
329	            return result
330	        kept = [position for position in collected.positions if position.position not in unresolved]
331	        partial = engine.evaluate(dataclasses.replace(collected, positions=kept))
332	        note = ("no bid was not taken as final: a catalogue group was not searched completely or facts are missing; "
333	                "position(s) " + ", ".join(unresolved) + " are left out instead")
334	        return dataclasses.replace(partial, issues=[*result.issues, note], omitted=[*partial.omitted, *unresolved])

528	def validate(answer: dict, schema: dict) -> list[str]:
529	    """A small JSON-schema check for the answer's shape: required fields, types, enums, extra fields."""
530	    problems = []
531	
532	    def check(value, rule, path):
533	        kind = rule.get("type")
534	        types = {"string": str, "number": (int, float), "integer": int, "object": dict, "array": list, "boolean": bool}
535	        if kind and not isinstance(value, types[kind]) or (kind in ("number", "integer") and isinstance(value, bool)):
536	            problems.append(f"{path}: expected {kind}")
537	            return
538	        if "enum" in rule and value not in rule["enum"]:
539	            problems.append(f"{path}: must be one of {rule['enum']}")
540	        if "const" in rule and value != rule["const"]:
541	            problems.append(f"{path}: must be {rule['const']!r}")
542	        if kind in ("number", "integer") and "minimum" in rule and value < rule["minimum"]:
543	            problems.append(f"{path}: below {rule['minimum']}")
544	        if kind == "object":
545	            for key in rule.get("required", []):
546	                if key not in value:
547	                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: required")
548	            props = rule.get("properties", {})
549	            for key, item in value.items():
550	                if key in props:
551	                    check(item, props[key], f"{path}.{key}")
552	                elif rule.get("additionalProperties") is False:
553	                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: not allowed")
554	        if kind == "array":
555	            for i, item in enumerate(value):
556	                check(item, rule.get("items", {}), f"{path}[{i}]")
557	
558	    check(answer, schema, "answer")
559	    return problems

"""Typed facts for one tender: the contract between the lead (which fills them from the sub-agents' reports) and the
bid engine (which turns them into the answer object, see `engine.build_bid`).

Every fact carries a `Source`: the website, document or record, date, sender and revision it was read from. The
engine uses dates, senders and references to apply the authority and time rules in code; the rest is for the log.

Conventions:
- Money and measures are `Decimal`. Build them with `dec()`, which also reads German and English number formats.
- Dates are `datetime` (timezone-aware, UTC preferred) or `date`. Build them with `when()`.
- A field that is `None` was not found. The engine never guesses it; it reports what is missing in `BidResult.issues`.
- Keys (Konditionsgruppe, tariff, commitment, pool, bonus, FX, index, end reserve) are compared after `norm_key()`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import functools
import re
import types
import typing
from dataclasses import MISSING, dataclass, field, fields, is_dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from enum import Enum

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provenance


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Source:
    """Where a fact was read. Only `date` and `sender` change the result; the rest is for traceability."""
    site: str = ""                       # site id from the run's access, e.g. the ERP's siteId
    document: str = ""                   # page, document number, message id or record id
    date: datetime | date | None = None  # when the record was issued (mail date, revision date, Q&A date)
    sender: str = ""                     # mail address of the sender, when it is a message
    revision: str = ""                   # document revision, when it is a versioned document
    note: str = ""                       # free text, e.g. the original wording of the value


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers (for whoever fills the facts)

_INVISIBLE = re.compile("[\u200b-\u200f\u2060\ufeff\u00ad]")  # zero-width, direction marks, soft hyphen


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", _INVISIBLE.sub("", text)).strip()


def clean(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove zero-width characters and collapse whitespace."""
    return _clean(str(text))


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def norm_key(text: str | None) -> str:
    """Canonical form of a code or key: no invisible characters or spaces, upper case."""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", "", clean(text or "")).upper()

FILLING_GUIDE = """How to fill the facts (the engine applies the bid rules; you only record what the sites show):

- tender_reference and scenario_date from the brief or the tender; bidder_domain from our own mailbox address;
  director_address = the sales director's address as the brief names it (without it, approvals from anyone count).
- Record what you read, not what you concluded. Keep superseded, withdrawn, look-alike and later records too, each
  with its own source: the engine picks the one that counts. Do not do any arithmetic yourself.
- Dates with their time and time zone: ISO 8601 with the offset the site states (2030-01-24T17:00:00+01:00) or in
  UTC; a time without a zone is read as UTC.
- source: for every mail value the sender's full address, the mail's date and time, and the exact tender reference
  it names (a reference with an extra suffix is another tender). For Q&A answers their number and date; for
  documents their revision.
- Quantities stay in the unit the tender or Q&A states (sets stay sets); the engine converts with the requirement's
  pieces_per_set. A Q&A answer that withdraws an earlier one goes into withdrawals with that answer's number.
- Requirements come from every revision you saw; mark the one the site marks as current/valid with current=true.
  A technical amendment names the revision and requirement it applies to; record it with that revision even if it
  is not the current one. For usable travel (nutzbarer Weg) enter the stated travel as stroke_mm, set
  usable_travel=true and the end-reserve key; the reserve comes from the matching Technikfreigabe record.
- Materials: every candidate from the ERP search, also inactive ones and near misses, with status, attributes,
  stock, lead times, carton size, masses in kg (625 g = 0.625), metal index code, setup fee and every price
  condition with its validity, currency, FX key, price unit and all quantity scales. List every Kataloggruppe you
  searched in searched_groups, also when the search found nothing.
- Keys that tie a position to a rule record (Konditionsgruppe, packaging tariff, delivery commitment, setup pool,
  project bonus) go into assignments, wherever you read them.
- Mail rule records: one record per key per mail. Konditionsgruppe wording -> scope base / base_and_surcharge /
  none. Metal indices with every validity window as stated. Bonus bands as lower/upper/percent. A setup pool's
  allocation = the listed method that matches the mail's wording.
- Discount: every approval-like mail for the tender with its sender, date, percent and any minimum order value; a
  mail that refuses or withdraws the discount is an approval with percent 0.
- Numbers as JSON numbers where you can; text numbers only with an unambiguous format. Unknown = leave it out
  (null); never guess. 0 only when the site states zero.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

        """One model step. A call can stall for minutes (a full queue, a stuck request); a fresh attempt usually
        returns quickly, so each attempt is capped and retried while the deadline allows. None: no answer in time."""
        for attempt in range(1, CALL_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            budget = self.deadline - WRAP_UP_RESERVE - time.time()
            if budget < 10:
                return None
            limit = min(CALL_SECONDS, budget)
            try:
                return await asyncio.wait_for(self.model.chat(messages, tools, temperature=0.2), timeout=limit)
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                self.stalls += 1

        return None

    async def _wrap_up(self) -> str:
        """The agent ran out of steps or time: one call without tools turns its notes into the usual report, so the
        lead model learns what was found and, as important, what was not checked."""
        notes = "\n".join(f"- {n}" for n in self.notes) or "(none)"
        pages = "\n".join(f"- {u}" for u in self.visited[-40:]) or "(none)"
        prompt = (f"# Task\n{self.task}\n\n# Notes you saved\n{notes}\n\n# Pages you visited\n{pages}\n\n"

                  "four parts. FOUND: each fact the task asked for that your notes contain, as `value (unit) — "
                  "source`. SUPERSEDED / LOOK-ALIKE: noted records that do not apply, with why. CHECKED, NOT "
                  "PRESENT: only what the notes show was searched completely and does not exist, with the evidence. "
                  "NOT CHECKED: everything else the task asked for, including newer versions, other folders, "
                  "further pages and unopened results, so nobody mistakes it for absent. Do not add facts that are "
                  "not in the notes. One short line per fact; no introduction.")
        timeout = min(WRAP_UP_SECONDS, max(30.0, self.deadline - time.time()))
        try:

                self.model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=WRAP_UP_TOKENS,
                                **_no_thinking(self.model)),
                timeout=timeout)
            if message.content:
                return "(written from notes after running out of steps or time)\n" + message.content
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            self.log(f"[{self.name}] wrap-up failed: {type(error).__name__} {error}")

"""The model behind the agent, through one OpenAI-compatible client. Switch it with environment variables only:

  AGENT_PROVIDER=qwen       (default) the hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
  AGENT_PROVIDER=anthropic  Claude via Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  AGENT_PROVIDER=openai     OpenAI (e.g. a Codex/GPT model): OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY
  AGENT_PROVIDER=openrouter any OpenRouter model: LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1, OPENROUTER_API_KEY
  AGENT_MODEL=<model id>    overrides the provider's default model

In a run every base URL already points at the platform's metering proxy; your own keys go in team secrets.
"""
import asyncio
import os
import time

from openai import APIError, APITimeoutError, AsyncOpenAI, RateLimitError

DEFAULT_MODELS = {
    "qwen": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
    "anthropic": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
    "openai": "gpt-5.5",
    "openrouter": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5",
}

# Longest lead call seen in a run was about 90 s; a call that hangs must not eat the run.
CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 240


def _client_config(provider: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Base URL and key of a provider. Every base URL comes from the run's environment, where it points at the
    platform's metering proxy; there is no address to fall back to."""
    env = os.environ
    if provider == "qwen":
        return env["QWEN_BASE_URL"], env["QWEN_API_KEY"]
    if provider == "anthropic":
        return env["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1", env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
    if provider == "openai":
        return env["OPENAI_BASE_URL"], env["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
    if provider == "openrouter":
        return env["LLM_PROXY_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/openrouter/v1", env["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]
    raise SystemExit(f"Unknown AGENT_PROVIDER {provider!r}; use one of {', '.join(DEFAULT_MODELS)}")


class Model:
    def __init__(self, provider: str | None = None, model: str | None = None, reasoning_effort: str | None = None):
        # how much the model thinks before it answers; None leaves the provider's default
        self.reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort
        self.provider = provider or os.environ.get("AGENT_PROVIDER", "qwen")
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODELS[self.provider]
        base_url, api_key = _client_config(self.provider)
        self.client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, max_retries=0)
        self.calls = 0
        self.prompt_tokens = 0
        self.completion_tokens = 0

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict] | None = None, **kwargs):
        """One completion with retries; returns the assistant message."""
        delay = 2.0
        for attempt in range(8):
            try:
                started = time.time()
                args = dict(model=self.model, messages=messages, **kwargs)
                if self.reasoning_effort:
                    args.setdefault("reasoning_effort", self.reasoning_effort)
                if tools:
                    args["tools"] = tools
                reply = await self.client.chat.completions.create(**args)
                self.calls += 1
                if reply.usage:
                    self.prompt_tokens += reply.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
                    self.completion_tokens += reply.usage.completion_tokens or 0
                if not reply.choices:
                    raise APIError("empty reply", request=None, body=None)
                reply.choices[0].message.elapsed = time.time() - started
                return reply.choices[0].message
            except (APIError, APITimeoutError, RateLimitError) as error:
                status = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
                if status in (400, 401, 403, 404) and attempt > 0:
                    raise
                print(f"[llm] {self.provider} call failed ({status or type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}); retrying", flush=True)
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay = min(delay * 2, 30)
        raise RuntimeError("model unavailable after retries")

    def usage(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.calls} calls, {self.prompt_tokens} prompt + {self.completion_tokens} completion tokens"

Both runs scored 10/100 for the same reason. The bid went in with an empty position list, so only the decision (5) and the tender reference (5) scored. Reading the sites isn't the main problem: in run_78afea, the first round already collected most of the facts except the ERP ones. The pipeline runs out of time before it gets the follow-up information that depends on other sites, and the engine then drops what it does know.

To read the latest code I fast-forwarded `stream-j` to `main` (not pushed). Nothing else changed, and the 180 unit tests pass.

## What happened in run_78afea

| Run clock | Event |
|---|---|
| 0:28 | Lead sends out 4 sub-agents |
| 0:28–3:45 | All 4 hit the 240 s limit. The ERP agent searched by product name because the catalogue groups weren't known yet, and found one material from a group the specification never names. |
| 3:40–4:30 | Writing the final reports: 2 of 4 timed out |
| 4:22–5:24 | Recorder turns the reports into facts (one call took 2.4 min) |
| **5:10–10:48** | **One lead model call: 5 min 38 s, 11,930 output tokens** |
| 10:49 | Lead sends 8 follow-ups (ERP per catalogue group, rule mails). All 8 are refused with "No time left". |
| 10:49–14:30 | Submission of an empty bid takes 3.7 min |

run_db0e went much the same way. Its second round started at 7:45 and had to end by about 9:00. After the 45 s set aside for the final report, each of the 9 sub-agents had about 30 s to browse, so all 9 did nothing useful. The mail report was never recorded, so the discount approval was lost. Submitting the empty bid took 6.5 minutes.

## Causes, most important first

1. **Reasoning is set to "xhigh" everywhere** ([agent.py:82-83](agent/agent.py#L82-L83)).
   - Qwen writes about 40 tokens/s, so 12k reasoning tokens means about 5 minutes.
   - The recorder uses the lead's model ([agent.py:219](agent/agent.py#L219)), so it also reasons at xhigh, just to copy facts into the schema.
2. **The lead's model call has no real time limit.**
   - It runs until the run's deadline ([agent.py:456](agent/agent.py#L456)).
   - The 240 s timeout in [llm.py:25](agent/llm.py#L25) did not stop the 5 min 38 s call.
   - The switch to submitting is only checked between lead calls ([agent.py:452](agent/agent.py#L452)), so a slow call also delays the submission. This is the same thing that made run_0ffb32ee end with no answer, so it puts eligibility at risk.
3. **Rounds don't fit a chain of dependencies.**
   - The ERP needs the catalogue groups from the specification, and those were known after 2.5–3.5 min.
   - ERP work only starts after the whole round, the recording and a lead call. It never got started in time.
   - All 17 investigations in both runs ended "stopped without finish".
   - Investigations that start with very little time left still run ([agent.py:187](agent/agent.py#L187)).
4. **The engine leaves out whole positions** ([engine/bid.py:113-118](agent/engine/bid.py#L113-L118)). A position without a material is dropped completely, even with a known quantity. Quantities for all 5 positions, including Q&A changes and the withdrawal, were in the facts. That is about 10 quantity points, plus probably the 5-point withdrawal check, all lost.
5. **Read data gets lost between steps:**
   - **Final report timeout (my stream).** A sub-agent stops browsing 45 s before its deadline to write its report ([browsing.py:52](agent/browsing.py#L52)). Qwen needs about 50 s for 2000 tokens, so 3 of 8 reports timed out.
   - **Last page not saved.** In db0e the specification table was read at 225 s, but the agent stopped before it saved a note, so it was lost.
   - **Unrecorded report.** The recorder failed on the mail report.
6. **The submission is slow and was never tried with positions.**
   - It took 3.7–6.5 min with nothing to configure.
   - It clicked the same button 5–6 times and had two 45 s stalls.
   - With 5 positions it will take longer.
7. **We don't know yet whether the engine is right on real data.** It has never priced a real position.

## Suggested changes (owner, pros and cons)

**S1. Lower reasoning effort and cap every call (O).**
- Lead on "low" or "medium" with a 60–90 s cap and a retry.
- Recorder with thinking off; sub-agents on "low".
- A separate timer that forces the submission on time, whatever the lead is doing.
- Pros:
  - About an hour of work, and it gives back about 5–6 minutes per run.
  - It removes the "no answer" risk.
- Cons:
  - The lead may plan less well. That matters less because the engine does the rule logic.
  - Needs one test run to confirm.

**S2. Send every position with what is known (I + O).** That means quantity, lead time and, if one exists, the closest material candidate.
- Pros:
  - About +10–15 points on these exact runs.
  - An empty optional field costs nothing.
- Cons:
  - `material_number` is required, and we don't know if the form accepts it empty. Test this locally with the scouting logins; those bids don't count.
  - Must not hide a real no-bid. The engine already keeps those cases apart.

**S3. Start follow-up work as soon as its input is known (O, using Ivan's `needed()`).** For example, the moment the catalogue groups are recorded, start one ERP investigation per group.
- Pros:
  - The ERP gets 6–8 minutes instead of 0.
  - No more waiting for a whole round, and the lead is no longer in the critical path.
- Cons:
  - The biggest rewrite on this list.
  - The fair-play reviewer could object to code deciding what to search. The search target comes from facts read at run time, and the sub-agent model still decides how to navigate. To be safe, a fast lead call can still phrase each task.
  - Needs facts recorded while sub-agents are still browsing (S5c).

**S4. More time per investigation; one long-lived agent per site (O + J).**
- Pros:
  - Login, cookie walls and consent gates happen once per site instead of once per task (about 30–60 s each).
  - The agent keeps what it learned about the site.
  - Also: don't start an investigation with less than about 2 minutes left.
- Cons:
  - A growing context slows each call, so old views have to be pruned.
  - Work on one site runs in sequence unless it uses a second tab.

**S5. Never lose what was read (J, my stream).**
- (a) A longer reserve for the final report, a shorter report, or a report built in code from the notes with no model call.
- (b) Attach the raw text of every document read to the report.
- (c) Send notes to the recorder as they are taken, not at the end.
- Pros: fixes the lost specification in db0e, facts arrive minutes earlier, and (c) makes S3 possible.
- Cons: bigger reports and more recorder calls, both cheap.

**S6. Sub-agents record typed facts themselves instead of notes (J + I + O).**
- Pros: removes the recorder step and the information lost in paraphrasing.
- Cons:
  - The facts schema is 26k characters and would be sent with every browsing step.
  - Qwen often gets nested JSON wrong.
  - The schema can't be cut per site, because the private dataset splits the information differently across the sites.
- S5c gets most of the benefit with less risk.

**S7. Prepare the submission early (O).** In a second tender-portal tab during collection: express interest, accept the documents and learn the form. Then time a 5-position submission and set the submit point from that measurement.
- Pros: a shorter, more reliable end phase.
- Cons: a signed wrong bid is final, so the early walk must be stopped in code before the final confirmation.

**S8. A 60-minute test run to measure the quality ceiling (O).** Test runs can last up to 2 hours.
- Pros: shows whether the facts and the engine are right when time isn't the limit, i.e. whether we are too slow or actually wrong.
- Cons: uses a test slot for an hour. The time switch must never reach a scored submission, so keep it in a separate package folder.

**S9. A stronger model for the lead and recorder, Qwen for browsing (team decision).**
- Pros:
  - Those few calls decide everything.
  - Better JSON from long reports, and no shared queue for those calls.
  - Cost × time is only a tie-break.
- Cons:
  - It goes against your "only Qwen" instruction.
  - It needs a team secret and Orhun's yes.
  - Each run would cost more, roughly $0.5–2 instead of $0.13.

**S10. Narrower tasks in the first round (O, prompt only).**
- Split the tender documents from the Q&A, and rule mails from approvals.
- The ERP agent first learns the search screens and gates, then waits for the catalogue groups instead of searching by name.
- Pros: uses the 4 tabs per site from the start, and it's cheap.
- Cons: more parallel calls means more queueing on Qwen.

## Recommended order

1. **Now (small, low risk):** S1, S2 (test the form locally first), S5a (mine), and no investigations with under 2 minutes left. Then one test run. I'd expect 25+ points and no stalls, but that's an estimate.
2. **In parallel:** S8, because it decides whether to spend the remaining time on speed or on correctness.
3. **Then the structural fix:** S3 + S5c + S7 together.
4. **S9:** only if the ceiling run shows Qwen gets facts wrong even with enough time.

+"""What the model client sends: thinking switched off, a token limit, a reasoning level."""
+import asyncio
+import os
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+
+import llm  # noqa: E402
+
+
+class FakeCompletions:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.sent = []
+
+    async def create(self, **args):
+        self.sent.append(args)
+        message = SimpleNamespace(content="ok", tool_calls=None)
+        return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=message)], usage=None)
+
+
+def sent(model: llm.Model, **kwargs) -> dict:
+    fake = FakeCompletions()
+    model.client = SimpleNamespace(chat=SimpleNamespace(completions=fake))
+    asyncio.run(model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], **kwargs))
+    return fake.sent[0]
+
+
+@patch.dict(os.environ, {"QWEN_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:9/qwen/v1", "QWEN_API_KEY": "local"})
+class Thinking(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_thinking_off_for_qwen(self):
+        args = sent(llm.Model(provider="qwen", thinking=False, reasoning_effort="xhigh"))
+        self.assertEqual(args["extra_body"]["chat_template_kwargs"]["enable_thinking"], False)
+        self.assertNotIn("reasoning_effort", args)
+
+    def test_existing_extra_body_is_kept(self):
+        args = sent(llm.Model(provider="qwen", thinking=False), extra_body={"top_k": 20})
+        self.assertEqual(args["extra_body"]["top_k"], 20)
+        self.assertFalse(args["extra_body"]["chat_template_kwargs"]["enable_thinking"])
+
+    def test_token_limit_and_reasoning_level(self):
+        args = sent(llm.Model(provider="qwen", reasoning_effort="low", max_tokens=4000))
+        self.assertEqual((args["max_tokens"], args["reasoning_effort"]), (4000, "low"))
+        self.assertNotIn("extra_body", args)
+
+    def test_a_call_may_set_its_own_token_limit(self):
+        args = sent(llm.Model(provider="qwen", max_tokens=4000), max_tokens=500)
+        self.assertEqual(args["max_tokens"], 500)

Ivan's `exp-speed` is merged into `stream-j`. Git could simply move the branch forward to his commit, so there was no merge commit and his Entire checkpoint stays as it is. There were no conflicts, and all 184 unit tests pass (including his 4 new ones). Nothing is pushed yet.

**What his branch changes** (it covers my S1 suggestion):
- **Sub-agents and submission agent** (browsing and filling the form): Qwen's thinking is off, which takes a step from about 10–13 s down to 2–3 s.
- **Recorder:** uses its own model with thinking off, capped at 8000 tokens. Until now it used the lead's xhigh model.
- **Lead:** reasoning is set to "low", with at most 4000 tokens and 120 s per call. A call that stalls is asked again instead of blocking until the end of the run, which removes the failure that cost us run_0ffb32ee.
- **ERP searches:** record the result list and open the details only for matching candidates.

**Risks I see:**
1. **The lead's 4000-token cap includes its reasoning.** In both runs the lead had to write facts itself with `add_facts`, and it also sent 8 long tasks at once. A cut-off answer gives broken arguments ("arguments were not valid JSON"), and nothing currently notices that the answer was truncated.
2. **The recorder's 8000-token cap has the same problem.** If one large report (all the Q&A answers and position keys) gets cut off, the retry probably gets cut off at the same point, and that report is lost.

   - A browsing call is only treated as stalled after 75 s ([browsing.py:53](agent/browsing.py#L53)), although a normal step now takes 2–3 s. About 25 s would be enough.

"""Stream J unit tests: a sub-agent stays on its own website, and its notes carry their source. Invented hosts only;
no browser, no model, no network."""
import asyncio
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from browser import Tab, origin  # noqa: E402
from browsing import BrowsingAgent  # noqa: E402


class FakePage:
    def __init__(self, url, title="A page"):
        self.url, self._title = url, title
        self.context = self

    def on(self, *args):  # Tab registers its event handlers here
        pass

    async def title(self):
        return self._title


def agent_for(*tabs):
    return BrowsingAgent(None, {t.site_id: t for t in tabs}, {}, "task", "context", name="t", deadline=0)


class OriginTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_origin(self):
        self.assertEqual(origin("https://Shop.Example.test:8443/a/b?c=1"), "https://shop.example.test:8443")
        self.assertEqual(origin("about:blank"), "")
        self.assertEqual(origin("/relative/path"), "")


class ForeignSiteTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        self.portal = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/login"))
        self.inbox = Tab("inbox", FakePage("https://inbox.example.test/"))

    def test_other_site_of_the_run_is_refused(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        refusal = asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("goto", {"url": "https://inbox.example.test/messages/7"}))
        self.assertTrue(refusal.startswith("Refused:"))
        self.assertIn("inbox", refusal)
        self.assertEqual(agent.refusals, 1)

    def test_download_from_other_site_is_refused(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        refusal = asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("download", {"url": "https://inbox.example.test/export.zip"}))
        self.assertTrue(refusal.startswith("Refused:"))

    def test_own_site_relative_and_unknown_hosts_pass_the_guard(self):
        agent = agent_for(self.portal)
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "/tenders?page=2"), "")
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://portal.example.test/docs/1"), "")
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://files.cdn.example.test/spec.pdf"), "")

    def test_an_agent_with_both_sites_may_use_both(self):  # the submission agent works portal and inbox
        agent = agent_for(self.portal, self.inbox)
        self.assertEqual(agent._foreign_site(self.portal, "https://inbox.example.test/"), "")


class NoteSourceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_note_is_stamped_with_site_page_and_source(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/doc/3", title="Spec, revision C"))
        agent = agent_for(tab)
        asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("note", {"facts": "Bore 42 mm", "source": "Spec rev C, 2030-01-02, status valid"}))
        asyncio.run(agent._run_tool("note", {"facts": "Stroke 99 mm"}))
        first, second = agent.notes
        self.assertIn("Bore 42 mm", first)
        self.assertIn("source: Spec rev C, 2030-01-02, status valid", first)
        self.assertIn('read on: portal · page "Spec, revision C" · https://portal.example.test/doc/3', first)
        self.assertIn("source: (not given)", second)
        report = agent._report("FOUND:\n- Bore 42 mm\nNOT FOUND:\n- nothing")
        self.assertIn("NOTES TAKEN WHILE BROWSING", report)
        self.assertIn("read on: portal", report)

class FakeCall:
    def __init__(self, n, name, arguments):
        self.id, self.type = f"call{n}", "function"
        self.function = type("F", (), {"name": name, "arguments": arguments})()


class FakeModel:
    """Browses forever with read_more (no page needed), then answers the tool-less wrap-up call."""

    def __init__(self, fail_wrap_up=False):
        self.seen, self.fail_wrap_up, self.n = [], fail_wrap_up, 0

    async def chat(self, messages, tools=None, **kwargs):
        self.seen.append([m.get("content", "") for m in messages if m["role"] == "user"])
        self.n += 1
        if tools is None:  # the wrap-up call
            if self.fail_wrap_up:
                raise RuntimeError("model down")
            return type("M", (), {"content": "FOUND:\n- Bore 42 mm — source: Spec rev C\nNOT FOUND:\n- stroke", "tool_calls": None})()
        return type("M", (), {"content": "", "tool_calls": [FakeCall(self.n, "read_more", '{"offset": 0}')]})()


class WrapUpTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        self.tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/doc/3"))

    def run_agent(self, model, steps):
        import time
        agent = BrowsingAgent(model, {"portal": self.tab}, {}, "Find the bore", "context", name="t",
                              deadline=time.time() + 600, max_steps=steps, log=lambda *_: None)
        agent.notes.append("Bore 42 mm\n  source: Spec rev C")
        agent.tabs["portal"].observe = self._observe
        return agent, asyncio.run(agent.run())

    async def _observe(self, offset=0):
        return "[portal] URL: https://portal.example.test/doc/3\nA page"

    def test_out_of_steps_gives_a_found_and_not_found_report(self):
        model = FakeModel()
        _, report = self.run_agent(model, steps=8)
        self.assertIn("written from notes", report)
        self.assertIn("NOT FOUND", report)
        self.assertIn("Bore 42 mm", report)  # the raw notes are still appended

    def test_failed_wrap_up_still_returns_the_notes(self):
        _, report = self.run_agent(FakeModel(fail_wrap_up=True), steps=3)
        self.assertIn("no report could be written", report)
        self.assertIn("Bore 42 mm", report)

    def test_nudges_to_note_and_to_finish(self):
        model = FakeModel()
        self.run_agent(model, steps=8)
        last_browse = model.seen[-2]  # user messages the model saw on its last browsing call
        self.assertTrue(any("without a note" in m for m in last_browse))
        self.assertTrue(any("steps left" in m for m in last_browse))

class StallingModelTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_stalled_model_call_is_retried(self):
        import time
        import browsing
        Tab.homes.clear()
        tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/"))

        async def observe(offset=0):
            return "a page"
        tab.observe = observe

        class StallsOnce:
            def __init__(self):
                self.calls = 0

            async def chat(self, messages, tools=None, **kwargs):
                self.calls += 1
                if self.calls == 1:
                    await asyncio.sleep(3600)  # the first request is stuck
                return type("M", (), {"content": "", "tool_calls": [FakeCall(self.calls, "finish", '{"report": "FOUND: x"}')]})()
        model = StallsOnce()
        old = browsing.CALL_SECONDS
        browsing.CALL_SECONDS = 0.2
        try:
            agent = BrowsingAgent(model, {"portal": tab}, {}, "task", "context", name="t",
                                  deadline=time.time() + 600, log=lambda *_: None)
            report = asyncio.run(agent.run())
        finally:
            browsing.CALL_SECONDS = old
        self.assertEqual(agent.stalls, 1)
        self.assertIn("FOUND: x", report)

class ReadsThenRunsOut:
    """Reads a page, optionally notes it, reads on until the steps are used up, then writes the wrap-up."""

    def __init__(self, note_after_first=False):
        self.n, self.note_after_first, self.wrap_up = 0, note_after_first, None

    async def chat(self, messages, tools=None, **kwargs):
        self.n += 1
        if tools is None:
            self.wrap_up = (messages[0]["content"], kwargs)
            return type("M", (), {"content": "FOUND:\n- stroke", "tool_calls": None})()
        if self.n == 2 and self.note_after_first:
            return type("M", (), {"content": "", "tool_calls": [FakeCall(self.n, "note", '{"facts": "Stroke 77 mm"}')]})()
        return type("M", (), {"content": "", "tool_calls": [FakeCall(self.n, "read_more", '{"offset": 0}')]})()


class UnnotedReadsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """What an agent read but had not noted when its time ran out still reaches the report."""

    def run_agent(self, model, steps, pages):
        import time
        Tab.homes.clear()
        tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/spec"))

        async def observe(offset=0):
            return "a page"
        tab.observe = observe
        tab.read_more = lambda offset=0: pages.pop(0) if pages else "end of page"
        agent = BrowsingAgent(model, {"portal": tab}, {}, "Find the stroke", "context", name="t",
                              deadline=time.time() + 600, max_steps=steps, log=lambda *_: None)
        return agent, asyncio.run(agent.run())

    def test_a_page_read_last_and_not_noted_is_passed_on(self):
        model = ReadsThenRunsOut()
        _, report = self.run_agent(model, 1, ["| Requirement | Stroke |\n| R-1 | 77 mm |"])
        self.assertIn("LAST PAGES READ, NOT NOTED YET", report)
        self.assertIn("| R-1 | 77 mm |", report)
        prompt, kwargs = model.wrap_up
        self.assertIn("| R-1 | 77 mm |", prompt)  # the wrap-up may report it as found
        self.assertEqual(kwargs["max_tokens"], 1000)

    def test_only_the_last_results_are_kept_and_a_note_clears_them(self):
        _, report = self.run_agent(ReadsThenRunsOut(), 4, ["first", "second", "third", "fourth"])
        tail = report.split("LAST PAGES READ, NOT NOTED YET")[1]
        self.assertNotIn("second", tail)
        self.assertIn("third", tail)
        self.assertIn("fourth", tail)
        _, report = self.run_agent(ReadsThenRunsOut(note_after_first=True), 2, ["| R-1 | 77 mm |"])
        self.assertNotIn("LAST PAGES READ", report)  # read, then noted: the note carries it

    def test_a_finished_report_carries_no_unnoted_pages(self):
        Tab.homes.clear()
        agent = agent_for(Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/")))
        agent.unnoted = ["read_more -> something"]
        agent.finished = True
        self.assertNotIn("LAST PAGES READ", agent._report("FOUND: x"))


class QuickStallTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_model_without_thinking_is_retried_sooner(self):
        import time
        import browsing
        Tab.homes.clear()
        tab = Tab("portal", FakePage("https://portal.example.test/"))

        async def observe(offset=0):
            return "a page"
        tab.observe = observe

        class QuickModel:
            thinking = False

            def __init__(self):
                self.calls = 0

            async def chat(self, messages, tools=None, **kwargs):
                self.calls += 1
                if self.calls == 1:
                    await asyncio.sleep(3600)
                return type("M", (), {"content": "", "tool_calls": [FakeCall(self.calls, "finish", '{"report": "FOUND: y"}')]})()
        old = browsing.CALL_SECONDS, browsing.QUICK_CALL_SECONDS
        browsing.CALL_SECONDS, browsing.QUICK_CALL_SECONDS = 600, 0.2
        try:
            agent = BrowsingAgent(QuickModel(), {"portal": tab}, {}, "task", "context", name="t",
                                  deadline=time.time() + 900, log=lambda *_: None)
            started = time.time()
            report = asyncio.run(agent.run())
        finally:
            browsing.CALL_SECONDS, browsing.QUICK_CALL_SECONDS = old
        self.assertLess(time.time() - started, 5)
        self.assertEqual(agent.stalls, 1)
        self.assertIn("FOUND: y", report)

"""The checklist of what is still missing (engine/needs.py): every gap the engine meets is named."""
import copy
import random
import unittest
from dataclasses import replace

from test_engine_base import core_facts
from test_engine_random import invent
from test_engine_robust import damage

from engine import evaluate


def unexplained(result) -> list[str]:
    """Positions left out or incompletely priced for which no "find" entry names the position or the whole bid."""
    needs = [n for n in result.needed() if n["kind"] == "find"]
    covered = {p for n in needs for p in n.get("positions", [])}
    global_need = any(not n.get("positions") for n in needs)
    return [p for p in result.omitted + result.incomplete if p not in covered and not global_need]


REMOVALS = {
    "fx rate": lambda f: f.fx_rates.clear(),
    "metal index": lambda f: f.metal_indices.clear(),
    "packaging tariff": lambda f: f.packaging_tariffs.clear(),
    "setup pool": lambda f: f.setup_pools.clear(),
    "project bonus": lambda f: f.project_bonuses.clear(),
    "condition group rule": lambda f: f.condition_groups.clear(),
    "delivery commitment": lambda f: f.delivery_commitments.clear(),
    "end reserve": lambda f: f.end_reserves.clear(),
    "price conditions": lambda f: [setattr(m, "conditions", []) for m in f.materials],
    "stock": lambda f: [setattr(m, "stock", None) for m in f.materials],
    "carton size": lambda f: [setattr(m, "pieces_per_carton", None) for m in f.materials],
    "allocation mass": lambda f: [setattr(m, "allocation_mass_kg", None) for m in f.materials],
    "surcharge mass": lambda f: [setattr(m, "surcharge_mass_kg", None) for m in f.materials],
    "materials": lambda f: (f.materials.clear(), f.searched_groups.clear()),
    "pieces per set": lambda f: [setattr(r, "pieces_per_set", None) for v in f.revisions for r in v.requirements],
    "current mark": lambda f: [setattr(v, "current", None) for v in f.revisions],
    "revisions": lambda f: f.revisions.clear(),
}


class Needs(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_complete_facts_need_nothing(self):
        result = evaluate(core_facts())
        self.assertTrue(result.complete)
        self.assertEqual([n for n in result.needed() if n["kind"] == "find"], [])

    def test_each_kind_of_missing_fact_is_named(self):
        for name, remove in REMOVALS.items():
            for seed in range(0, 300, 15):
                with self.subTest(removed=name, seed=seed):
                    facts = copy.deepcopy(invent(seed).facts)
                    remove(facts)
                    result = evaluate(facts)
                    self.assertEqual(unexplained(result), [])
                    if result.omitted or result.incomplete:
                        self.assertFalse(result.complete)

    def test_damaged_facts_gaps_are_named(self):
        for seed in range(200):
            with self.subTest(seed=seed):
                result = evaluate(damage(copy.deepcopy(invent(seed % 300).facts), random.Random(seed)))
                self.assertEqual(unexplained(result), [], result.issues)

    def test_examples(self):
        f = core_facts()
        f.director_address = ""
        f.materials = [m for m in f.materials if m.catalogue_group != "G-B"]
        f.materials[0] = replace(f.materials[0], conditions=[])
        needs = {n["what"]: n for n in evaluate(f).needed()}
        self.assertIn("director_address: the sales director's mail address", needs)
        search = next(n for w, n in needs.items() if w.startswith("search Kataloggruppe G-B"))
        self.assertEqual((search["kind"], search["site"], search["positions"], search["rule"]),
                         ("find", "ERP", ["2"], 10))
        self.assertTrue(any(w.startswith("price conditions of M-A1") for w in needs))

    def test_no_bid_asks_for_a_recheck(self):
        f = core_facts()
        f.materials = [m for m in f.materials if m.material_number != "M-B1"]
        f.searched_groups = ["G-B"]
        result = evaluate(f)
        self.assertEqual(result.answer["decision"], "no_bid")
        self.assertTrue(any(n["kind"] == "verify" and "no_bid" in n["what"] for n in result.needed()))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.

In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
"""
import json
import os


def cdp_urls(env=os.environ) -> list[str]:
    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
    try:
        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
    except ValueError:
        urls = []
    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])


async def connect(playwright, number: int = 0):
    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
    urls = cdp_urls()
    if urls:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(urls[number])
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
    else:
        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1")
        context = await browser.new_context()
    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    return browser, page

"""Debug harness (scratchpad only, never packaged): runs the agent's own submission step against the public
scouting sites with a test answer, and writes every page view the submission agent gets to a dump file.

usage: uv run --no-sync python submit_probe.py <agent dir> <dump file> <answer json file> [seconds]
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright  # noqa: E402

import agent as lead_module  # noqa: E402
import browsers  # noqa: E402
import engine  # noqa: E402
import run as contract  # noqa: E402
import submission  # noqa: E402
from browser import Tab  # noqa: E402
from llm import Model  # noqa: E402

DUMP, ANSWER = sys.argv[2], json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
SECONDS = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 360


async def main():
    task, _ = contract.load_run()
    model = Model(thinking=False)
    out = open(DUMP, "w", encoding="utf-8")
    original = submission.SubmissionAgent._run_tool

    async def logged(self, name, args):
        result = await original(self, name, args)
        out.write(f"\n===== [{time.time() - started:5.0f}s] {name} {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False)}\n{result}\n")
        out.flush()
        return result
    submission.SubmissionAgent._run_tool = logged

    started = time.time()
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        tabs = {}
        for access in task["access"]:
            if access["siteId"] not in ("tender-portal", "mail"):
                continue
            _, page = await browsers.connect(pw, 0)
            await page.goto(access["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            tabs[access["siteId"]] = Tab(access["siteId"], page)
        lead = lead_module.Orchestrator(task, None, tabs, model, started, model)
        lead.deadline = time.time() + SECONDS
        lead.priced = engine.BidResult(ANSWER["answer"], omitted=ANSWER.get("omitted", []))
        report = await lead.submit(lead.priced.answer, "")
        out.write("\n===== REPORT\n" + report + "\n")
        print(report)


asyncio.run(main())

"""Debug harness (scratchpad only): signs in to the public webmail with the scouting login and times what the page
view sees afterwards, to reproduce the "Loading .../consent" hang. usage: mail_probe.py <agent dir> [rounds]"""
import asyncio
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright  # noqa: E402

import browsers  # noqa: E402
import run as contract  # noqa: E402
from browser import Tab  # noqa: E402
from browsing import BrowsingAgent  # noqa: E402

ROUNDS = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 3


async def main():
    task, _ = contract.load_run()
    access = next(a for a in task["access"] if a["siteId"] == "mail")
    async with async_playwright() as pw:
        for round_ in range(ROUNDS):
            browser, page = await browsers.connect(pw, 0)
            requests = []
            page.on("request", lambda r: requests.append(f"{time.time() - t0:5.1f}s {r.method} {r.url}")
                    if r.resource_type == "document" else None)
            page.on("response", lambda r: requests.append(f"{time.time() - t0:5.1f}s <- {r.status} {r.url}")
                    if r.request.resource_type == "document" else None)
            t0 = time.time()
            await page.goto(access["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            tab = Tab("mail", page)
            agent = BrowsingAgent(None, {"mail": tab}, {"mail": access["credentials"]}, "", "", name="probe",
                                  deadline=time.time() + 300, log=print)
            view = await tab.observe()
            print(f"--- round {round_}: first view {time.time() - t0:.1f}s:", view.splitlines()[:3])
            if "consent" in page.url or "Cookie" in view:
                b = next((l for l in view.splitlines() if "akzeptieren" in l.lower()), "")
                print("consent first:", b[:120])
            t1 = time.time()
            result = await agent._login(tab)
            print(f"login took {time.time() - t1:.1f}s; url {page.url}; title {await tab._title()!r}")
            print("   ", result.splitlines()[:4])
            for i in range(3):
                t2 = time.time()
                view = await tab.observe()
                print(f"observe {i}: {time.time() - t2:.1f}s url {page.url} lines {len(view.splitlines())}:",
                      [l for l in view.splitlines()[:4]])
            print("document requests:\n  " + "\n  ".join(requests))
            await browser.close()


asyncio.run(main())

- **Short chain:** the chain gets so short that it fits the time we actually have.

**Step 1: an answer that is always complete (engine, Ivan's file).**
- Every position of the bill of quantities is always in the bid, and each field is filled the moment its inputs are known:
  - **quantity:** from the tender and the Q&A;
  - **material:** the matching ERP material, otherwise the best candidate;
  - **base price, lead time, surcharges:** each on its own, when its inputs exist;
  - **unit price and total:** from what is known, with arithmetic that adds up.

    `recorder` decides what the recorder's calls return, one entry per call."""

    def __init__(self, recorder, recorder_delay=0.0):
        self.recorder, self.recorder_delay = list(recorder), recorder_delay
        self.lead_calls, self.states = [], []

    async def chat(self, messages, tools, **kwargs):
        forced = kwargs.get("tool_choice", {}).get("function", {}).get("name")
        if len(tools) == 1:  # the recorder has only add_facts

            update = self.recorder.pop(0) if self.recorder else {}
            if isinstance(update, Exception):

        if len(self.lead_calls) == 1:

**What still goes wrong:** the ERP searches by catalogue group only started at 407 s, leaving them about 90 s of browsing before investigations end at 540 s. Prices, stock and confirmed materials from the ERP would again have been mostly missing. Three things made the ERP start that late:

- **The first four jobs never finished on their own.** Each ran to its 4-minute limit (207–216 s) instead of returning early with a narrow result.
- **Recording was slow:** 9 s for the ERP report, 41 s for the specification, 79 s for the tender portal and 122 s for the mail.
- **The lead was busy at the wrong moment.** Its turn from 262 s to 382 s went into writing all the facts out itself with `add_facts`, although the prompt says it should only correct facts. It started nothing in that turn, so it missed the specification being recorded at 288 s. It only started the ERP searches in its next turn, at 407 s.

**What the change did fix:** the bid no longer ends up empty. From 382 s it held all 5 positions with their quantities (25, 29, 16, 21 and 110 pieces, including a set converted to pieces). Before, at the same point, it had 0 positions. Their materials would have been chosen in the form from the requirements, but that part never ran because I cancelled before the submission.

The changes are only in my working copy of `stream-j`: they're not committed or pushed, and `main` and the other branches are untouched. The local run's log is in `scouting/local-core-1.log`, which is ignored by git.

## The new concept: three jobs, no hand-offs

**What failed every time:** information was handed from model to model. Site agent, report, recorder, lead, the next agent, a new login: every hand-off cost minutes and lost information, and the important ERP step always came last.

**The new idea:** split the work by *what has to be found*, not by *website*. Each job runs from start to finish in one agent, so its dependency chain stays inside one agent and nothing has to be handed over. Three agents start at second 0 and run in parallel. Each can open all four websites.

| Agent | Job | Records |
|---|---|---|
| **A: positions** | bill of quantities, all Q&A answers | positions, quantity changes, withdrawals, amendments, keys per position |
| **B: materials** | specification (current revision), **then itself** searches the ERP by each catalogue group and opens the matching materials (status, stock, prices) | requirements, catalogue groups, materials, conditions |
| **C: rules** | every message for the tender reference | discount approvals, rule mails, end reserves, rates |

- **No lead model and no rounds.** The three jobs are fixed from the brief. Where to go and what to search is still the agents' own choice, which keeps it within fair play.
- **No recorder and no report writing.** Agents save typed facts directly with a `record` tool while they browse, each only its own part of the facts. A fact is in the moment it is read, and nothing is lost when time runs out.
- **The one cross-site dependency** (specification → ERP) stays inside agent B. The others (end reserves, amendments, keys) are worked out by the engine from the facts, so no agent waits for another.
- **At minute 9** the engine prices whatever is known, every position included (the "always complete" answer is ready), and the existing submission agent enters it. It signed a bid with 5 priced positions in 487 s locally.

**What I reuse** because it works: the browser tools, the engine, the submission agent. **What disappears:** the lead, the recorder, the wrap-ups and all the waiting between agents.

**What I considered and dropped:** one single agent doing everything in order. It's even simpler, but it would need about 150 steps in a row, with a growing context and Qwen stalls. That's too risky for 20 minutes.

**The main risk:** agent B's chain (specification about 2 min, then 4 ERP groups) has to fit into 9 minutes. If it doesn't, the positions are still bid with their quantities and the materials chosen in the form.

1. **Concept:** go ahead with "three jobs, no hand-offs", or do you want the single agent?
2. **Model:** only Qwen as before, or may agent B (the hardest job) use a stronger model through the proxy?
3. **Branch:** I'd create `stream-j-simple` from `stream-j` and bring the uncommitted always-complete engine into it, since the new concept needs it. Is that OK, or should it start from `main`?
